subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns enforce tool-result-backed verification, fail-closed diagnostics, or documented non-verification when visible final text claims side effects?
rationale: The current code deliberately supports automatic final delivery and message-tool-only suppression, so adding generic claim verification would affect channel UX, privacy, fallback behavior, and existing direct-message semantics.

options.title: Define verification policy
options.body: Require a maintainer-approved tool-result ledger or diagnostic before delivering visible success claims for actions that should have side effects.

options.title: Limit scope to delivery-tool gaps
options.body: Treat missing source delivery when the message tool is omitted as the platform-owned class and leave broader side-effect verification to prompts or hooks.

options.title: Document current boundary
options.body: Document that OpenClaw transports model final text but does not verify arbitrary claimed side effects without a future plugin or hook policy.

recommendation.title: Define verification policy
recommendation.body: Require a maintainer-approved tool-result ledger or diagnostic before delivering visible success claims for actions that should have side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the closest policy change and have the strongest current source-reply ownership signal in the inspected history.
